input.summary: Make the mutual cap the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, and confirm Excluded Claims sit outside the cap.
input.comment: [Playbook] We reset the cap to our standard position — the greater of twelve months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, mutual for both Parties — because a one-month fee cap is not a meaningful remedy against a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year commitment. We also removed "without exception" so the Excluded Claims in Section 21.3 (indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement) remain uncapped as that Section intends; a flat twelve months' Fees cap is our fallback if the USD floor is an issue.

ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, which are not subject to any limitation of liability, each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
